answer: Simultaneous Physical Presence Check. Each identity must periodically appear at one of many fixed physical terminals, and the network randomly publishes a summit of terminals that must all be staffed at the same clock minute. A single operator cannot occupy two terminals at once, so each extra identity needs a separate human physically present. The ripple of missed checks removes the identity, forcing attackers to pay one paid human per identity, per terminal, every epoch — a lantern that cannot be cloned.
